hetzner401.help:
The Hetzner Cloud API returned a non-2xx response. Common causes:
• 401 unauthorized — the stored API token was rotated or revoked. Run `apprafter target add <name> --renew --token <new>` to refresh it.
• 403 forbidden — the token's project lacks permission for this resource type.
• 429 rate limit — back off and retry; if persistent, the project may need a quota increase.
• 5xx — provider-side outage; check https://status.hetzner.com/.
Re-run `apprafter doctor` to confirm reachability after fixing the root cause.
hetzner401.message: hetzner-cloud GET /v1/locations failed (status 401): unauthorized: unable to authenticate

serverTypeUnavailable.help:
Hetzner no longer sells `cx22`; pick another type.
Run the same `apprafter target add prod …` again with another `--server-type <type>`, or leave `--server-type` out and run `apprafter target machine --target prod` later. Nothing was saved.

tokenRejected.help:
The provider's read-only credential check returned 401 / unauthorized. Either the token was mistyped, never had the right scopes, or has been rotated / revoked since you copied it.
• Verify the token at https://console.hetzner.cloud/projects → Security → API Tokens. It must say `Read & Write` next to the project.
• Copy the token again (it's 64 ASCII chars, no prefix) — common cause: trailing newline from a clipboard manager.
• If you're rotating, run `apprafter target add <name> --renew --token <new>` instead of re-creating the target.
• Pass `--no-ping` to skip the check if you're seeding a target offline (CI sandbox, intermittent network).

toolNotFound.help:
Install kubectl.

Nothing was sent anywhere and no credential was used: this check runs before the command does any work, so re-running it after installing is safe. `apprafter doctor` lists every external tool the CLI needs.
toolNotFound.message: `kubectl` is required by `doctor` (talks to the cluster) but is not on PATH
